newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine peso closes higher on unchanged rate.
newsitem.headline: Philippine peso closes higher on unchanged rate.

text.p: *Central Bank still out of the market
The Philippine peso gained on Tuesday to 26.336 from 26.341 after the Central Bank left its key overnight borrowing rate unchanged at 10.0 percent.
"It just range traded. All are adopting a wait-and-see attitude because the Central Bank might still lower its overnight rate," a dealer said.
The peso moved from 26.340/26.335, with the day's average at 26.338 from 26.339.
Volume fell to $190.20 million from $265.10 million.
"The Central Bank is lying low," another dealer said, adding that it wants to prevent peso speculation.

Dealers said they are not discounting a further cut in the Central Bank's overnight borrowing rate since the 91-day T-bill rate of 9.804 percent is below the Central Bank's overnight rate of ten percent.
The Central Bank did not intervene in the market but it quoted a lower bid and offer rate for the dollar at 26.28/26.345 from 26.29/26.35, dealers said.
